transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Patel (Opal CTO), Sarah Gomez (Opal Head of Security), Diego Ramos (Opal Infra)

Summary (auto): quick demo of Redwood Console and API retention controls, discussion of PII redaction, request storage toggles, and audit logs. Next steps captured.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood - AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today, really appreciate it. Quick intro - I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Mark (Opal - CTO): Good, thanks. We've got about 45 minutes, hopefully good to cover retention controls and compliance stuff.
00:12 Priya (Redwood - SE): Awesome. We'll start with a short walkthrough of the Console, then show API toggles, and finish with Optimize suggestions for batching/costs.
00:20 Sarah (Opal - Security): Great. Primary ask is: How do we ensure PII isn't stored, and can we control retention per-endpoint?
00:28 Jordan: Absolutely - that's the goal for this demo. We'll show the request storage toggle, auto PII redaction, and audit logs with KMS key support.

02:05 Priya (Redwood - SE): Opening the Console now - Home > Projects > Opal-pay. On the right you see Data Controls tab. The transcription might say "data control" but it's Data Controls.
02:18 Priya: We have three main levers: request storage (on/off), automatic redaction (PII detectors), and retention windows (30/90/365/custom).
02:35 Diego (Opal - Infra): Can retention be set per-route? We have payments routes vs analytics routes.
02:40 Priya: Yep, per-route settings. You can set a policy at project, route, or model variant level. In the UI I'll click the payments-api route - here I toggle Request Storage: Off. Note: turning off request storage prevents requests/inputs from being persisted in our long-term store; ephemeral logs for debugging still available for X hours if you enable short debug window.
03:10 Sarah: When you say "ephemeral logs" is that encrypted? Where are they stored?
03:16 Priya: They're encrypted at rest and in transit. We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private deployments; for hosted we have managed KMS but can integrate with AWS KMS for VPC. Also audit logs are exported to your S3/CloudWatch or partner SIEM via a push.
03:45 Mark: Does turning request storage off affect embeddings/knowledge caching? Like will KV cache still happen?
03:52 Priya: Good question. The KV cache (k-v cache) is separate at runtime; request storage toggles control persisted request logs and dataset retention, not the in-memory kv cache used for latency. For background we do have prefix caching and continuous batching but that stays internal and doesn't write persistent request content when storage is off.

05:10 Jordan: Quick qual - what's your compliance posture? SOC 2? Data residency?
05:15 Sarah: We're SOC 2 Type II in progress, PCI scope for card processing, prefer EU region for EU customers. Also SSO via our IdP and SAML.
05:24 Jordan: Good - Redwood supports SSO/SAML and RBAC. We'll include our SOC2 and encryption docs after the call.

07:00 Priya: Back to the demo - automatic PII redaction. In the Data Controls you can select detectors: emails, credit cards, SSN, phone numbers, custom regex. Turn on "Mask PII in transcripts" or "Redact before storage." If redact-before-storage is enabled, we run detectors at ingest and replace detected spans with tokens (e.g., <REDACTED_PHONE>).
07:38 Diego: How accurate are the detectors? We have lots of edge cases with masked PANs.
07:45 Priya: Detectors are high-precision but not perfect; for sensitive workloads we recommend combining automated redaction with a small post-processing ruleset you can add as a policy. Also we offer a PII review mode where redactions get flagged to your team for manual verification (in private deployments).
08:20 Sarah: Is redaction done client-side or server-side? We don't want raw text leaving our environment.
08:27 Priya: For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers you can enable local pre-processing with our SDK so detection/redaction happens within your network before the request hits our control plane. For hosted, detection happens server-side - we do have contract and MDRs around that.

10:05 Priya: Now the API view - here's the typical request payload. You can set header x-redwood-request-storage: off to ensure storage disabled for that call. We also support a per-request redact: true flag which triggers immediate redaction irrespective of route defaults.
10:30 Mark: So we can toggle storage on a per-request basis via header? Good. What about logs - do we still get request IDs for debugging?
10:36 Priya: Yes, request IDs and aggregated telemetry are still emitted for observability; the payloads may be scrubbed depending on storage settings. We also offer a short-lived debug window - you can enable it for X hrs and it's automatically purged.

13:00 Jordan: Time to cover audit trails - Priya?
13:05 Priya: Audit logs capture configuration changes, who toggled settings (SAML identity), and stored to your audit sink. They include metadata about completed redactions and retention policy applied. If you need immutable logs we can support append-only export to your S3 with object locking (for Dedicated).
13:36 Sarah: Do logs include redacted content or the original?
13:40 Priya: By default logs will include redaction tokens, not original content. For compliance needs we can set up encrypted vaulting accessible only via customer-managed keys in Private/Dedicated. That's when we can store originals but only if you provide an HSM/KMS and retention policy allows.

16:10 Diego: Performance question - if we enable server-side PII redaction, what's the latency hit? Some of our endpoints are sub-200ms.
16:20 Priya: It depends on model and detector path. For text-only detectors we typically add 10-30ms per request for short sequences. For heavy regex and long inputs that can grow. In our Optimize tool we recommend batching and quantization profiles for different routes; for latency-sensitive routes we suggest offloading redaction client-side or using lightweight detectors. We can run a benchmark for your sample traffic.

18:05 Mark: Cost impact? If we keep storage on vs off, or keep retention long, how do we calculate costs?
18:12 Jordan: Primary costs are token spend (inference) and storage. Storage is billed per GB-month plus retrieval if you're archiving. Retention windows directly affect the stored GB. We can provide an estimator - we'll share a pricing example in the next email. Also Redwood Optimize will flag hot routes and suggest shorter retention for high-volume, low-value routes.

21:00 Priya: Quick show of the API logs - console shows anonymized example: "Request id: abc123, route: payments-charge, redaction: true, retention: 30 days" - you can click to see the redaction map and what fields were masked. There may be minor typos in the UI copy.

23:40 Sarah: For PCI, do we need full cardholder data removed or tokenized?
23:46 Priya: Redwood doesn't store full PAN by default; our detectors will redact card numbers. For PCI scope reduction we recommend tokenization client-side and ensuring card data never reaches our runtime. If you need tokenization we can discuss partners or a reference architecture.

26:10 Priya: Now switching to Dedicated/VPC options - in Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools, and you can choose customer-managed KMS, private control plane, and on-prem packaged option. That enables local redaction and ensures no data leaves your VPC.
26:40 Mark: That's promising. What about logging retention for audit - can we set immutable retention for e-discovery?
26:47 Priya: Yes, for Dedicated we support object locking and export to a write-once S3 bucket in your account. For hosted, we can ship to your export endpoint but immutability is limited by host-managed store.

29:00 Diego: Any enterprise connectors for SIEM? We use Splunk.
29:05 Priya: We have Splunk and Datadog export connectors, plus webhooks to push structured audit events.

31:15 Jordan: Quick pause, any other high-level questions?
31:20 Mark: Timeline - we want a pilot in April for a single route with sample traffic. Can Redwood support a 1-week benchmark with our sample prompts?
31:27 Jordan: Yes - typical pilot: baseline metrics, cost/latency, then one week of throughput tests. We'll coordinate pricing and capacity.

33:00 Priya: Now one last feature - programmatic policies. You can declare a retention policy as YAML via the API and apply it to multiple routes. Example snippet shown: retention: 30d, redact: true, detectors: [card,email,ssn]. That helps with scale.
33:32 Sarah: Nice. Is there a dry-run mode? We want to test redaction accuracy before moving to redact-before-storage.
33:38 Priya: Yes - dry-run mode logs detected spans without altering storage, helpful for tuning detection thresholds.

36:10 Jordan: Let's talk risk tradeoffs - if you want zero risk of sensitive data persistence, the safest path is client-side redaction + Dedicated with customer-managed keys. Hosted can do a lot but has more managed pieces.
36:30 Mark: Understood. We'll evaluate cost of Dedicated vs hosted with storage off and client-side redaction for critical routes.

38:50 Priya: A couple of gotchas to call out: 1) Per-request headers override route defaults, but if you do batch calls be mindful of concatenated inputs exposing PII across items. 2) Embeddings created from PII content can be persistent - we have embedding retention controls too.
39:20 Diego: Embeddings retention - can we disable embedding storage while keeping request logs?
39:26 Priya: Yes - embedding storage is controlled separately. You can disable vector persist for particular models or routes.

41:40 Sarah: Do you support deletion requests for e.g., GDPR?
41:45 Priya: Yes - we support subject access and deletion workflows. You can request batch deletion by request ID or by associated user ID; we provide audit proof of deletion. For Dedicated we can provide API tokens that perform deletions within your VPC.

44:10 Jordan: Wrapping up - recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2 + security whitepaper and details on KMS integration. Priya will run the baseline throughput test with sanitized sample data and share a spreadsheet. Mark to provide prompt set and retention policy requirements. We also agreed to target pilot week of 2026-04-13.
44:40 Mark: Sounds good. One more thing - any docs on our end for pre-processing redaction SDK?
44:45 Priya: Yes, we'll include the SDK example (Node/Python) for client-side redaction.

46:00 Sarah: Quick note - competitors we evaluated were Anthropic and OpenAI endpoints, mainly around redaction and private deployments. Concern was about closed models' logging controls.
46:12 Jordan: Got it - we'll include a short comparison doc.

47:30 Diego: Thanks everyone.
47:33 Jordan: Thanks - we'll follow up with the docs and pricing.
47:38 Priya: I'll kick off the benchmark once we get the sample.
47:40 Mark: Okay talk soon.

Auto-generated topics (end): Data retention, PII redaction, Request storage toggles, Audit logs, Dedicated/VPC options

Action items (in-transcript): Jordan to send security whitepaper; Priya to run throughput baseline; Mark to share prompt set.
